items.subject: Recipe db drift (index vs specs) - round 2 of the bounced artichoke half
evidence: audit-db-agreement.ps1 2026-09-01 about 12:45: exactly 5 issues, exit 1, all HEAD-INGREDIENT drift, e.g. 'italian-sausage-minestrone line 7 says Artichoke Hearts, 36.5 oz (1032 g), the card says Artichoke Hearts (Hannaford), 36.5 oz (1032 g)'. As-found state verified at HEAD 10f5856b: all five specs carry display '(Hannaford)', stored BARE JSON-LD, bare cost_lines; no uncommitted spec edits.

food-macros-db.json 'Artichoke Hearts': brand 'Great Value', source 'USDA FDC 2313271 (Branded) QUARTERED ARTICHOKE HEARTS (Wal-Mart Stores, Inc.), fetched 2026-09-01', notes 'The previous row was Hannaford'. The five display lines were built under the previous brand; the current ' (Great Value)' suffix cannot strip ' (Hannaford)'.

DECISION (b) PRICE IS RIGHT: the built card pricing blob for the casserole reads {item: 'Artichoke Hearts', disp: 'Artichoke Hearts (Hannaford)', bid: 'artichoke-hearts', gpu: 28.350, pkg_g: 240, pkg_l: '13.8oz can'}. The live cheapest prices by bid from smp-feed, whose artichoke-hearts row is $0.1615/oz Walmart = $2.22 per 13.75 oz can, matching the specs' static cost_lines ('Buy 3 13.8oz cans: $6.68' = $2.227/can); pkg_g 240 is the CURRENT Great Value drained-can basis recorded in the DB note. Hannaford is not among the feed's 7 stores. This is a wrong brand NAME on live cards, with a correct price and basis.

DECISION (a) CONVENTION: the brand parenthetical IS the card convention, not an accident: 5,512 of 7,845 display lines carry the current DB brand suffix, and build-v2-spec.ps1 line 245 appends it (dropping only fresh/store brands, and clearing it when the display item is renamed, line 246). The correct display is therefore 'Artichoke Hearts (Great Value)', a brand correction, not a brand removal.

WHAT ELSE THE MECHANISM LETS THROUGH, measured over all 584 specs / 7,845 display lines (post-strip display name vs scaler item): 65 mismatches in FOUR classes. (i) The 5 artichoke lines: stale Hannaford, the only ones the agreement audit can see. (ii) 9 'Tortilla (La Banderita)' lines + 1 'Panko Breadcrumbs (Kikkoman)' line: the SAME stale-brand class baked into BOTH sides. Stored JSON-LD verified on all 10 (e.g. chipotle-sweet-potato-pork-chili head list holds 'Tortilla (La Banderita), 29.25 oz (830 g)'), all 10 in published-hashes.json, so TEN live pages ship a wrong brand in the visible list AND in Google structured data while audit-db-agreement reads them as agreement forever, because stored equals derived. Tortilla DB brand is 'Great Value' (the 2026-08-06 GV Small Fajita recalibration; a reader buying La Banderita buys a product the card does not price); Panko Breadcrumbs DB row has NO brand. (iii) 47 'Milk (store brand)' lines: the paren EQUALS the current DB brand string 'store brand', which the fresh/store filter drops on append and strip today; legacy-cosmetic, NOT stale, measured silent under the new check, left alone. (iv) 3 reader renames (Frozen Peas / Green Olives / Cheddar Cheese): by design per build-v2-spec line 246, left alone.

SELF-TEST BLINDNESS: the repair own real-spec case asserts 'the JSON-LD list now matches the card line for line' (repair-head-ingredients.ps1 line 221); agreement with the card is the success criterion, so writing the stale brand into the spec PASSES it. audit-db-agreement head check (lines 314-333) compares stored vs derived, so the baked-in 10 are structurally invisible to it.

-Slugs BUG: param([string[]]$Slugs) + '$Slugs -contains $_.BaseName' (lines 32, 233); via powershell -File a comma-separated list arrives as ONE string and line 234 throws 'no specs matched'. engine\publish.ps1 has the same [string[]]$Slugs shape, so the publish step must be invoked in-session (real array) unless it gets the same split.
items.root_cause: Get-HiBrandSuffix strips the brand parenthetical by exact match against the CURRENT food-macros-db brand, so any display line built under a PREVIOUS brand becomes unstrippable the moment the DB row swaps brands - a rule silently disarmed by the world moving. Every consumer then inherits the blindness in its own way: repair-head-ingredients derives the JSON-LD FROM the display line, so it actively writes the stale brand into the authored source; audit-db-agreement measures AGREEMENT between stored and derived, so once both sides carry the stale brand (the 10 tortilla/panko lines) the defect is permanently green; and the repair self-test asserts agreement with the card, the exact criterion the corruption satisfies. Nothing anywhere compared the display line brand against the source of truth (the DB row), so a brand swap left 15 live pages naming a brand the pricing does not buy, and only 5 of them could ever page.

surface_fix.what: correct the 15 stale display-line brands to the current food-macros-db brand, re-derive the JSON-LD on the 10 specs where the stale brand is baked into both sides, rebuild and republish the 15 cards
surface_fix.exact_change: In ingredients_display ONLY, one line per spec: 'Artichoke Hearts (Hannaford)' -> 'Artichoke Hearts (Great Value)' in the 5 artichoke specs; 'Tortilla (La Banderita)' -> 'Tortilla (Great Value)' in the 9 tortilla specs; 'Panko Breadcrumbs (Kikkoman)' -> 'Panko Breadcrumbs' in turkey-meatballs-cream-sauce-skillet (its DB row has no brand, so the builder appends nothing). The changed text is plain ASCII inside the \u003cstrong\u003e escaped display strings: edit the raw bytes, NEVER round-trip the spec through ConvertFrom-Json then ConvertTo-Json (SPEC-SCHEMA standing rule; the repair script key-scoped write exists for that reason). Do NOT hand-edit head.recipeIngredient anywhere: the 5 artichoke stored lists are already correct (bare) and must not change; the 10 tortilla/panko stored lists get rewritten by repair-head-ingredients -Apply AFTER the hardening in root_fix ships. Then rebuild the 15 cards with pipeline\build-card2.ps1 and publish via engine\publish.ps1 -Slugs (in-session array) with its live verify.
surface_fix.expected_intermediate: repair-head-ingredients -Apply over the 15 slugs must report EXACTLY 10 rewritten (one JSON-LD line each, stale brand removed to the bare name) and 5 already correct. Any other split is an unmeasured find: stop.

root_fix.what: one check in the ONE copy of the derivation (head-ingredients-lib) so a stale brand paren can neither be written by the repair nor stay invisible to the audit: the derived name is compared against the source of truth (the current DB brand), not against the other derived copy
root_fix.exact_change: (1) head-ingredients-lib: new Get-HiRawBrand($FoodDbMap,$CanonItem) returning ($d.brand -split '/')[0].Trim() with NO fresh/store filtering, empty string when the row or brand is absent. (2) In Get-HeadRecipeIngredient, after the existing suffix strip: let $item = [string]$ing[$k].item; if $name differs from $item and $name -match ('^' + [regex]::Escape($item) + '\s+\((.+)\)$'), compare the captured paren text to Get-HiRawBrand for the canon; on mismatch THROW 'stale brand parenthetical (X) on ITEM - food-macros-db brand is now Y or none; fix ingredients_display and rebuild the card, never hand-edit the JSON-LD'. Measured over the whole catalog this fires on exactly the 15 stale lines and is silent on the 47 Milk (store brand) lines (paren equals the raw current brand), the 3 renames (no item-plus-paren shape), and BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (name equals item). The repair inherits REFUSAL through its per-spec try/catch (spec goes to errs, exit 1, NO write), so it can never again be satisfied by corrupting its own reference; audit-db-agreement inherits PAGING through its catch at line 318, which reports the throw text per spec even when stored equals derived, making the baked-in class visible for the first time. Get-HiBrandSuffix itself is untouched. (3) repair-head-ingredients: before the BaseName filter, split -Slugs on commas: if($Slugs){ $Slugs = @($Slugs | ForEach-Object { $_ -split ',' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ }) } - PS 5.1 safe, a real array passes through unchanged.

Price was never wrong - the cards price bid artichoke-hearts at the Great Value can. Hardened Get-HeadRecipeIngredient to THROW on any brand paren that mismatches the current DB brand, so the repair refuses the write and the audit pages the baked-in class; fixed the -Slugs comma split. Cards rebuilt and republished; audit-db-agreement 0 issues, honestly.

items.deviation: Six deviations, five of them additive and one of them a live bug this ship uncovered and had to fix before the ship could land. (A) THE PLAN'S SHIP SEQUENCE WORKED AS WRITTEN. Step 2 hard stop cleared exactly: after the hardening, audit-db-agreement -ShowAll paged EXACTLY 15 specs, every one a stale-brand refusal, naming the same 15 slugs (5 Hannaford, 9 La Banderita, 1 Kikkoman). Step 4 split exactly 10 rewritten / 5 already correct / 0 errors. Step 5 returned issues=0, exit 0, honestly green over 584 recipes. (B) -Slugs SPLIT HOISTED INTO A FUNCTION. The plan prescribed an inline one-liner in repair-head-ingredients. Same semantics, but placed in a named pure function Expand-HrSlugList so -SelfTest can actually REACH it (standing rule: a fix ships with a test that can exercise it). Four frozen cases now cover it. (C) A THIRD COPY OF THE -Slugs TRAP. engine\build-cards.ps1 has the identical param([string[]]$Slugs) + BaseName filter shape and dies on 'no specs match -Slugs'. Same class the plan already understands, so it was fixed the same way and noted rather than bounced. All three were then driven live through `powershell -File` with a comma list and all three worked. (D) THE LOADED GUN WAS PROVED DISARMED, NOT REASONED ABOUT. repair-head-ingredients -Apply was run against the REAL pre-fix bytes of italian-sausage-minestrone (taken from git HEAD into a scratch tree, not a hand-made fixture): it reported 'rewritten 0 | already correct 1 | errors 1', exit 1, printed the stale-brand refusal, and the file came back byte-identical by md5. It can no longer write the defect into the source of truth. (E) NEW MECHANISM FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE SHIP: engine\publish.ps1 -VerifyOnly STAMPS THE PUBLISH JOURNAL. Line 294 called Save-PubHashes on every successful verify with no -VerifyOnly guard, and the verify only checks title, paywall and schema presence, never CONTENT. So a read-only pass wrote 'these local bytes are live' about bytes that had never been sent. Measured, not inferred: a -VerifyOnly pass over the 15 rebuilt cards stamped the 14 that verified; the real publish then reported 'published+verified OK: 1 / 15 (skipped-unchanged: 14)'; and a cache-busting fetch confirmed thriftycrew.com/turkey-migas-skillet still served 'Tortilla (La Banderita)' and /italian-sausage-minestrone still served 'Artichoke Hearts (Hannaford)'. The single slug whose verify FAILED was the only one that actually shipped. The `if(-not $VerifyOnly){ Save-PubHashes }` at the bottom of the file was written to prevent this and could not, because the write already happened per slug inside the loop. Fixed by guarding the in-loop stamp; the 15 were then republished with -Force, 15/15 OK, and all 15 live pages re-verified clean. Recorded as its own memory class. (F) TWO SIDE OBSERVATIONS, both checked and both benign. The -VerifyOnly VERIFY FAIL on turkey-huevos-rancheros-rice-bowls was a -VerifyOnly artifact, NOT a paywall leak: line 155 skips the existence GET under -VerifyOnly, so $liveVis falls back to the stale spec default instead of the live 'public' the free rotation set on 2026-08-31, and a legitimately free page then reads as unpaywalled. Under the real publish it verified OK. And the rebuild refreshed the build-time 'Three more for this week' block on 8 of the 15 cards; that block is deterministic from recipes-db, v2-perserving and free-rotation.json, all of which moved since those cards were last built, and all 45 resulting links were checked against published-hashes.json (580 entries): every one points at a published recipe, none at the 4 in-flight specs.
items.post_ship_correction: POST-SHIP CORRECTION (orchestrator, 2026-09-01, after commit 4df85ee0). Commit 4df85ee0 message contains two FALSE claims; this field is the correction and it wins. (1) It says the 15 cards were rebuilt but NOT republished. They WERE republished and are live: all 15 verified 200 on www.thriftycrew.com with the corrected brand and zero occurrences of Hannaford, La Banderita or Kikkoman. (2) It says thriftycrew.com was returning Cloudflare 403 sitewide and the Ghost Admin API was unreachable. The SITE WAS NEVER DOWN. The orchestrator probed the APEX domain only; the site is served from www.thriftycrew.com, which is canonical in the canonical tag, og:url and every sitemap URL, and which was healthy throughout. The apex genuinely does return Cloudflare Error 1000 in a real browser, but that is a separate and much smaller problem (type-in traffic and old apex backlinks), it is of unknown age, and the 11:30-to-13:20 window the commit message asserts is an artifact of the same mistake and should be ignored. It is parked needs-brad as a Cloudflare dashboard change. (3) Consequently the 15 publish-journal entries the orchestrator cleared were NOT false stamps. The journal was restored from backup to 580 entries and verified, so no card republishes needlessly. THE CODE IN 4df85ee0 IS UNAFFECTED AND CORRECT: the stale-brand throw and the -VerifyOnly watermark bug were both measured from the source and both stand. LESSON: verifying a fix on the wrong hostname is the same class as measuring the wrong corpus. The estate has no watcher that asserts the live site serves 200, and if it grows one it must pin the CANONICAL host, because the apex would have paged every day for a site that was fine.
